title: The Martyrdom of Polycarp
hookLine: the oldest account of a martyr outside the New Testament
tomorrow: who wrote a whole Sunday service down for an emperor to read?

lines: A WORD THROWN, A WORD THROWN BACK.
cards: Some insults get flipped. A word thrown at a group becomes the word they throw back. In a stadium in Smyrna, a crowd is chanting at the Christians: away with the atheists.
They've arrested the old bishop, Polycarp, and the governor offers him a way out: just say it. Away with the atheists. And Polycarp says it.
He looks hard at the packed stands, waves his hand toward the crowd, groans, looks up to heaven, and says: away with the atheists. Why would a bishop say that?

teach.h: THE SAME WORDS, AIMED AT THE CROWD.
teach.b: First, the flip. In the story, atheists is the crowd's name for the Christians, who won't swear by Caesar or honor the city's gods. Polycarp says the words, but with his hand pointed at the crowd.
Same words, opposite aim. Second, the answer. The governor presses: swear, curse Christ, and I'll let you go.

teach.h: HE NEVER DID ME ANY INJURY.
teach.b: Polycarp answers, in the old Schaff translation: "Eighty and six years have I served Him, and He never did me any injury." How could he curse his King, who saved him? Third, the fire.
Threatened with fire, he says theirs burns for an hour and goes out.

When it's lit, the letter says, the flames arch around him like a ship's sail filled with wind, and he is like bread baking. The story ends with his death, told plainly and without cruelty. Fourth, the letter itself.
His church in Smyrna wrote all of it down and sent it to another church, and to the communities of the holy and catholic Church in every place, asking them to pass it on.
Some readers call it the oldest martyr story we have outside the New Testament. His friends gathered his bones as more precious than jewels, and planned to keep the day he died as a birthday.

how: Catholics keep Polycarp's feast each year and name martyrs in their prayers; many parishes also pray in the intercessions for people persecuted for their faith.

games.q: what does “the martyrdom of polycarp” mean?
o: a sermon Polycarp preached before his arrest
the rule Polycarp wrote for his church in Smyrna
a letter telling how Polycarp died as a witness

p: the crowd's chant, turned back on them
arched around him like a sail

s: when told to say 'away with the atheists,' Polycarp refused
he said it, but with his hand waved toward the crowd.
the story reaches us as a letter from Polycarp's own church
the church in Smyrna wrote it and asked that it be passed on.
the letter is addressed only to the church in Smyrna
Smyrna sent it out, to another church and to the holy and catholic Church in every place.

games.q: your teammate's family offers her a paid summer trip if she stops going to Mass. she's served at that parish for years. what's Polycarp's kind of answer?
o: a kind no: what she's served for years has never done her wrong.
take the trip now and quietly go back to Mass afterward.
say yes; old loyalties shouldn't cost anybody a summer.
games.why: offered his freedom for one sentence, Polycarp answered from his whole life: he had served Christ for years and never been wronged. how could he curse his King?

practice: Bring to mind one place where people are hurt or threatened for what they believe, whatever their faith. Say its name out loud, slowly, once every few breaths.
Polycarp's church wrote so faraway strangers would remember; if you pray, let each name be a prayer for them.

wordCard.voice: The Martyrdom of Polycarp. A letter from his own church: an old bishop who would not curse the King he had served.

orig.note: Greek for a witness or testimony: the word this letter's title is built on.

carryVoice: Pocket this one: the oldest story, written down so the next church would hear it too. Until tomorrow.

sources.tr: Schaff, Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1 (Roberts and Donaldson)
sources.q: Eighty and six years have I served Him, and He never did me any injury
